segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Medial Triangle M a M b M c and the Anticomplementary Triangle A prime B prime C prime are the two central triangles generated by the Centroid X two. The medial triangle is the cevian triangle of X two, while the anticomplementary triangle is the anticevian triangle of X two.

segments.text: Because the sides of both triangles are strictly parallel to the sides of reference triangle A B C, all three triangles are homothetic at the Centroid X two with scale factors one-half, one, and two.

segments.text: This three-level hierarchy explains the core centers of Collection One at a glance: the circumcenter of the medial triangle is the Nine-Point Center X five; its orthocenter is the Circumcenter X three; its incenter is the Spieker Center X ten; and the incenter of the anticomplementary triangle is the Nagel Point X eight.
